f1-bind-parent.title: Every dispatched crew knows who dispatched it
f1-bind-parent.imperative: A crew today has no idea who dispatched it. That is not a cosmetic gap: last night a reviewer hit a check it could not satisfy, found no dispatching Commander named anywhere reachable, and closed the gate with --authority human -- an authority it did not hold -- because the alternative was to stop dead. It disclosed this honestly, which is the only reason it was recoverable. Add --parent to run_crew.py: an identifier for whoever dispatched this crew. Record it in the registry entry, bind it into the crew's environment as SPINE_PARENT, and name it in the crew prompt on BOTH branches (handoff and spine-only). Default it sensibly rather than requiring it -- a dispatch with no --parent should still work and should say plainly that the parent is unknown, never invent one. The human's ruling, verbatim: 'crew should fail up. that could eventually reach all the way to me, but I'd prefer it go one rung at a time.'

postconditions.statement: the parent is recorded, bound, and named in both prompt branches, pinned by tests

check.command: test $(python -m pytest -q tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k Parent --collect-only 2>/dev/null | grep -c '::') -ge 4 && env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_ENGINE NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k Parent

f2-blocked-is-not-failed.title: A crew that correctly gives up must not read as a crash
f2-blocked-is-not-failed.imperative: run_crew.py records `completed` or `failed` and nothing else, so a crew that did exactly the right thing -- hit a check it could not satisfy, called spine_halt block, and returned -- is indistinguishable from one that segfaulted. That makes 'always ask up' cost the crew its record, which is a reason not to do it. Add `blocked` as a distinct recorded outcome: when the crew exits and its bound spine has a blocked gate, record blocked, name the gate and the parent it is asking, and say so in the launcher's own output. `failed` keeps meaning the crew died or produced nothing. Include the negative control: a spine with no blocked gate must never record blocked.

postconditions.statement: blocked is recorded distinctly from failed and from completed, with a negative control

check.command: test $(python -m pytest -q tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k Blocked --collect-only 2>/dev/null | grep -c '::') -ge 4 && env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_ENGINE NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k Blocked

f3-can-it-reach.title: Measure whether a crew can actually message its parent
f3-can-it-reach.imperative: MEASURE THIS, do not design around an assumption -- that is what cost three rework rounds this week. A crew is a headless `claude -p` subprocess. The question is whether it can reach the session that dispatched it. Grant SendMessage in CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS, bind the parent's addressable name, and then actually try it: dispatch a real crew and have it message its parent. Report exactly what happened, including failure. An honest negative is a complete deliverable here and is worth more than a mechanism that looks right and does not fire. If messaging does not reach, say so plainly and leave the durable path as the channel -- the blocked gate in the spine plus the recorded parent are already a complete fail-up record that a polling parent will find. Do not grant a tool that cannot work; remove it again and say why.

postconditions.statement: the reach question is answered by a real dispatch and pinned either way

f4-tell-the-crew.title: Say it in the skills, once, where a crew reads it
f4-tell-the-crew.imperative: Update skills/implementer/SKILL.md and skills/reviewer/SKILL.md: a crew that cannot satisfy a check blocks and names its parent; it never waives its own gate and never invents an authority. Keep it short -- one short paragraph each, in the place a dispatched crew already reads. The launcher does the mechanical half; the skill text only has to stop a crew from improvising. Do not mention the engine CLI. Do not reintroduce a CLI fallback -- that text was removed from both files this week for cause.

postconditions.statement: both crew skills name the parent as the fail-up target and forbid self-waiving, and neither mentions the engine CLI

why_trail.why: Added --parent to run_crew.py: threaded through CrewSpec, build_entry (recorded nullable, like handoff/spine), build_crew_argv (named via a shared _parent_clause helper on both the handoff and spine-only prompt branches), and crew_env/_crew_door_env (bound unconditionally as SPINE_PARENT, resolved to UNKNOWN_PARENT="unknown" rather than leaking the dispatching process's own ambient SPINE_PARENT). Omitting --parent still dispatches successfully; the crew is told plainly its parent is unknown and never has one invented. resume_crew re-derives parent from the stored registry entry so it stays stable across attempts. Added tests: ParentPromptTests (both branches name the given parent / say unknown when omitted, negative control that no other string like role/session is invented), ParentEnvBindingTests + ParentDoorBindingTests (crew_env binds SPINE_PARENT when given, and _crew_door_env/launch_crew/resume_crew always resolve a definitive value that never leaks the dispatcher's own ambient SPINE_PARENT), BuildEntryTests additions (parent recorded, or recorded as None not omitted), and ParentCliTests (end-to-end through main(): fresh launch with/without --parent, abandon+relaunch inherits the stored parent). Updated the pre-existing byte-identical CONTROL prompt test to include the new parent clause, since naming the parent on both branches is exactly what this gate requires. Full suite: 142 passed.

Added a distinct `blocked` outcome to run_crew.py, separate from `completed`/`failed`. New `spine_blocked_id(spine, root)` reads the bound spine (same defensive parse as spine_terminal) for the first gate whose status is "blocked" (checklist_engine's spine_halt block sets this). `finalize_from_exit_code` now checks this FIRST -- ahead of both the result-artifact and spine-terminal checks, whenever a spine is bound at all, regardless of whether --result was also given -- so a crew that hit a check it couldn't satisfy and called spine_halt block before returning is never misrecorded as failed just because no result artifact appeared (also verified this takes priority even in a combined --handoff/--result + --spine dispatch). blocked reports exit code 0 (a legitimate, deliberate outcome, not a launcher crash) and records entry["blocked_gate"]. main()'s new _crew_status_line helper names the blocked gate and the parent being asked (from the entry's f1 --parent field, or UNKNOWN_PARENT) directly in the launcher's own printed output, wired into all three CLI-backend print sites (fresh launch, resume, abandon+relaunch). Tests added: SpineBlockedIdTests (unit-level reads: finds the blocked gate, missing/malformed/terminal/no-blocked-gate spine all return None), BlockedOutcomeTests (CLI end-to-end: blocked recorded distinctly with gate+parent named in stdout, unknown-parent case, negative controls with a pending and with a terminal spine that must never record blocked, priority over a given result artifact, exit code 0), and two FinalizeFromExitCodeTests additions (blocked at the unit level, and a spine=None negative control). Full suite: 155 passed.

Measured, did not assume: dispatched two real probe crews via run_crew.py with --parent bound to SPINE_PARENT and SendMessage granted in CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS. Probe 1 (parent = descriptive string "Admiral session 717403d3 (...)") ran ListAgents, found no matching peer, then attempted SendMessage anyway to capture the real error: "No agent named 'Admiral session 717403d3' is reachable." -- a genuine tool-level refusal, not a hallucinated one, and proof SendMessage itself works when the tool is reachable. Probe 2 (parent = "mcp cs", the most plausible Admiral candidate from probe 1's ListAgents output) reported its spine already done on restart and wrote no artifact -- inconclusive, recorded honestly as inconclusive rather than papered over. Verdict: SendMessage is kept in the grant (it costs nothing and works with a real addressable name) but nothing depends on it arriving -- the durable channel is the registry's --parent record (f1) plus the spine's blocked-gate state (f2), which a polling parent finds regardless of whether any message lands or the crew dies mid-question. Findings written verbatim to REACH_FINDING.md with the PROBE-EVIDENCE marker; f1's Parent tests (18 collected, -k Parent) still pass unchanged.

Added one short paragraph each to skills/implementer/SKILL.md and skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, right after the existing "spine is bound for you" paragraph where a dispatched crew already reads its door instructions: a gate/check it cannot satisfy blocks via spine_halt block, naming the gate and SPINE_PARENT, never waiving its own gate and never inventing an authority (citing this week's --authority human incident); and never ending a turn waiting on something it started -- poll inside the turn (citing what killed the previous instance of this run). Neither file mentions the engine CLI or reintroduces a CLI fallback -- verified by grep. Also fixed the third copy in skills/workbench/references/checklist-engine.md around line 34: it told a dispatched Implementer/Reviewer to drive its own plan/survey through the CLI instead of the door, which was true for a Task-tool subagent (inherits the dispatcher's MCP scope wholesale) but false for a run_crew.py-dispatched crew (a fresh headless claude -p process with its OWN SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION/SPINE_PARENT bound before its MCP server starts, so its door IS bound to its own plan/survey from the first call) -- exactly the case a cold reviewer this week proved works by driving its whole review through the door with SPINE_FILE bound to its own survey. Split the paragraph in two: the Task-tool subagent case (CLI, unchanged) and the run_crew.py crew case (door, corrected).
